h3. *Description of problem:*

* This was reported in [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CRW-11431?focusedCommentId=17525513|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CRW-11431?focusedCommentId=17525513|smart-link].
* This was implemented for [https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23826|https://github.com/eclipse-che/che/issues/23826|smart-link] 

When a user restarts the workspace (after a change in the devfile) the gateway is supposed to automatically reconnect to the remote IDE. This fails at times with the following timeout:

!image-20260708-112328.png|width=321,alt="image-20260708-112328.png"!



*Workaround*: manually reconnect

h3. *Prerequisites (if any, like setup, operators/versions):*

* Devspaces 3.29
* Gateway plugin 0.0.16

h3. *Steps to Reproduce*

# ASSERT: have a workspace running that has a devfile
# EXEC: in the remote IDE: modify the devfile and pick “Restart Workspace (Devfile)” in the editor context menu or in the context menu of the file. Then confirm the restart.
# ASSERT: the remote IDE is closing and back in the Gateway list of workspaces you can see how the workspace is stopped and restarted.

 

h3. *Actual results:*

At times (not always) the Gateway errors with a timeout and wont reconnect to the remote IDE.

!image-20260708-112328 (90d5f4be-eb74-4215-9f3c-790b458d362f).png|width=321,alt="image-20260708-112328.png"!

h3. *Expected results:*

Gateway should reconnect and have the remote IDE opened again.

h3. *Reproducibility (Always/Intermittent/Only Once):*

Always

h3. *Acceptance criteria:* 

 The user should get back to the remote IDE as documented.

*Definition of Done:*

Gateway successfully reconnects and the user has the remote IDE opened after the restart.

h3. *Build Details:*

h3. *Additional info (Such as Logs, Screenshots, etc):*

 

h3.  *

This was reported in [https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CRW-11431?focusedCommentId=17525513|https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/CRW-11431?focusedCommentId=17525513|smart-link] :

When a user restarts the workspace (after a change in the devfile) the gateway is supposed to automatically reconnect to the remote IDE. This fails at times with the following timeout:

!https://media-cdn.atlassian.com/file/5451deb2-df90-435e-8822-380d475ebb0a/image/cdn?allowAnimated=true&client=73cd193a-75ff-4ccf-9bc9-33cd784f6d2b&collection=&height=125&max-age=2592000&mode=full-fit&source=mediaCard&token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..V_noEt5azOYjm705hHUacE61dn3h0FqC81cNozrLQ1E&width=321#media-blob-url=true&id=5451deb2-df90-435e-8822-380d475ebb0a&clientId=73cd193a-75ff-4ccf-9bc9-33cd784f6d2b&contextId=&collection=|width=250,alt="image-20260708-112328.png"!

h3. *Prerequisites (if any, like setup, operators/versions):*

* Devspaces 3.29
* Gateway plugin 0.0.16

h3. *Steps to Reproduce*

# ASSERT: have a workspace running that has a devfile
# EXEC: in the remote IDE: modify the devfile and pick “Restart Workspace (Devfile)” in the editor context menu or in the context menu of the file. Then confirm the restart.
# ASSERT: the remote IDE is closing and back in the Gateway list of workspaces you can see how the workspace is stopped and restarted.

 

h3. *Actual results:*

At times (not always) the Gateway errors with a timeout and wont reconnect to the remote IDE.

!https://media-cdn.atlassian.com/file/5451deb2-df90-435e-8822-380d475ebb0a/image/cdn?allowAnimated=true&client=73cd193a-75ff-4ccf-9bc9-33cd784f6d2b&collection=&height=125&max-age=2592000&mode=full-fit&source=mediaCard&token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9..V_noEt5azOYjm705hHUacE61dn3h0FqC81cNozrLQ1E&width=321#media-blob-url=true&id=5451deb2-df90-435e-8822-380d475ebb0a&clientId=73cd193a-75ff-4ccf-9bc9-33cd784f6d2b&contextId=&collection=|width=250!

h3. *Expected results:*

Gateway should reconnect and have the remote IDE opened again.

h3. *Reproducibility (Always/Intermittent/Only Once):*

Intermittent

h3. *Acceptance criteria:* 

 The user should get back to the remote IDE as documented.

*Definition of Done:*

Gateway successfully reconnects and the user has the remote IDE opened after the restart.

h3. *Build Details:*

h3. *Additional info (Such as Logs, Screenshots, etc):*

h3. *Description of problem:*

When your kube config points to a a different cluster than the one you want to connect to, connecting via link fails.

!image-20260707-152342.png|width=437,alt="image-20260707-152342.png"!

Workaround: 

* make sure {{current-context}} points to the cluster that you want to connect to
* use the approach where you select the cluster, list the available workspaces and then connect

h3. *Prerequisites (if any, like setup, operators/versions):*

# use plugin version 0.0.16
# have {{current-context}} in your local kube config pointing to a different cluster

h3. *Steps to Reproduce*

# EXEC: create a new workspace with JetBrains editor
# EXEC: when the workspace is ready and you get the welcome page, click onto the link that opens it in gateway
!image-20260707-152636.png|width=662,alt="image-20260707-152636.png"!
# ASSERT: Gateway opens the connection settings with cluster, token 
(note: *another bug*: the preselected cluster is not the one that your workspace runs on. I created one in staging, connection settings page came up with the first cluster available in my kube config, which is sandbox. Correcting it does not help) 
# EXEC: Click  “OK”

h3. *Actual results:*

Connecting fails with the error shown below:

!image-20260707-152342.png|width=437,alt="image-20260707-152342.png"!

h3. *Expected results:*

You should be able to connect to your workspace from the welcome page that you get when the workspace was created.

h3. *Reproducibility (Always/Intermittent/Only Once):*

Always

h3. *Acceptance criteria:* 

You should be able to connect to your workspace from the welcome page that you get when the workspace was created.

*Definition of Done:*

Bug is fixed, connecting works as documented.

h3. *Build Details:*

h3. *Additional info (Such as Logs, Screenshots, etc):*

items.toString:
Currently, OpenVSX is exposed via a dedicated Ingress/Route with its own hostname (openvsx-<namespace>.<base-domain>). This introduces an extra DNS record and TLS certificate requirement per deployment. Ideally, OpenVSX should be accessible at <che-host>/openvsx, served through the existing Che gateway — consistent with how other Che components are exposed.

Known blockers from initial investigation:

* The OpenVSX WebUI is a Vite-built React SPA with base defaulting to '/'. All static assets (JS bundles, CSS) are referenced with absolute root paths (e.g., /bundle-xxx.js), so they return 404/418 when served under a path prefix like /openvsx.
* The server itself has no server.servlet.context-path configured; it expects to run at root /.
* Upstream deployment (eclipse-openvsx) also uses a standalone Route/Ingress at root /.

Areas to investigate:

# Vite base configuration — Can the webui be rebuilt with base: '/openvsx/' so all asset referencesbecome prefix-aware? What changes are needed in the custom image build?
# Spring Boot server.servlet.context-path — Setting /openvsx as the context path for the server side. Verify API endpoints, health checks, and webui asset serving still work correctly under the prefix.
# Che gateway (Traefik) rewriting — Can Traefik StripPrefix or ReplacePath middleware transparently strip /openvsx before forwarding to the server, so the server still sees root paths? Does this work for both API calls and static asset loading?
# Hybrid approach — API calls go through the gateway with path stripping, while the webui is reconfigured to be prefix-aware.
# Impact on VS Code extension marketplace endpoint — IDE clients currently use OpenVSXURL to fetch extensions. Verify that changing the URL to a path-based scheme doesn't break marketplace resolution in editors.
Team A: Dashboard, devfile and plugin registries, open-vsx, devfile-converter, image-puller, server, gateway, authentication, try-in-web-ide action, telemetry

items.toString:
= Workspace startup fails on IBM Z with OpenShift Container Platform 4.22

On IBM Z (s390x) clusters running OpenShift Container Platform 4.22, workspace startup fails with a `FailedPostStartHook` error. This issue affects {prod-short} with {devworkspace} Operator 0.42 on OpenShift Container Platform 4.22. Earlier versions of {prod-short} (3.28.0, 3.28.1, 3.28.2) with {devworkspace} Operator 0.41 on OpenShift Container Platform 4.22 are also affected.
+
Workspaces start successfully on IBM Z with OpenShift Container Platform 4.16 and 4.21, and on x86_64, arm64, and IBM Power architectures with OpenShift Container Platform 4.22.

.Workaround

To work around this problem, patch the `DevWorkspaceTemplate` resource to bypass the `postStart` hook and start the IDE entrypoint directly:

. Patch the `DevWorkspaceTemplate` to remove the `postStart` event and add a direct entrypoint command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc patch devworkspacetemplate __<template-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ --type=json -p '[
  {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/events/postStart"},
  {"op": "add", "path": "/spec/components/1/container/args", "value": ["/bin/sh", "-c", "nohup /checode/entrypoint-volume.sh > /checode/entrypoint-logs.txt 2>&1 & exec tail -f /dev/null"]}
]'
----

. Restart the workspace:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc patch devworkspace __<workspace-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"started":true}}'
----

h4. *Context / Current Limitation:*

Currently, the {{devspaces-multicluster-redirector}} acts as a static rule-matching engine. It evaluates user routing strictly based on a linear sequence of group mappings derived from the OpenShift/Keycloak OAuth token.

While this works perfectly for static 1:1 mappings or displaying an interactive selection screen for users belonging to _distinct_ groups, it presents a major structural limitation: *We cannot dynamically distribute or load-balance users belonging to the same unified production group across multiple clusters.* If we attempt to duplicate a group name in the configuration with different target URLs, the linear loop exits on the first match (_First-Match-Wins_), rendering subsequent target clusters unreachable.

h4. *Proposed Enhancement:*

We want to evolve the Redirector from a *Static Rule Engine* to a *Stateful, Load-Aware Router*. The component should be capable of intercepting a single group and dynamically making routing decisions based on real-time infrastructure metrics (cluster occupancy, active workspace density, etc.) instead of relying solely on raw group-text matches.

= Restrict workspace override fields and improve stability with DevWorkspace Operator 0.42.0

DevWorkspace Operator 0.42.0 introduces configurable field-level restrictions for container and pod overrides, along with fixes for OpenShift registry RoleBinding accumulation, nested project cloning, PVC cleanup pod security context, init-persistent-home memory limits, and ephemeral workspace home volumes.

.Configurable field-level restrictions for container and pod overrides

Cluster administrators can define deny rules in `DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig` to block specific fields or field values from being set via the `container-overrides` and `pod-overrides` DevWorkspace attributes. Restrictions are specified using the new `config.overrides.restrictedContainerOverrideFields` and `config.overrides.restrictedPodOverrideFields` fields.

On Kubernetes, a set of security-sensitive fields are denied out of the box including privileged containers, running as root, host networking, and `hostPath` volumes—matching the restrictions that OpenShift enforces natively via SCCs. These defaults can be adjusted from the global `DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig` object.

[source,yaml]
----
apiVersion: controller.devfile.io/v1alpha1
kind: DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig
metadata:
  name: devworkspace-operator-config
  namespace: $OPERATOR_INSTALL_NAMESPACE
config:
  overrides:
    restrictedContainerOverrideFields:
      - securityContext.privileged
      - securityContext.runAsUser
    restrictedPodOverrideFields:
      - hostNetwork
----

See link:https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/blob/main/docs/dwo-configuration.md#restricting-override-fields[restricting override fields] for configuration details.

.OpenShift registry image-puller RoleBinding no longer accumulates deleted workspace ServiceAccounts

OpenShift registry image-puller RoleBindings no longer accumulate deleted workspace ServiceAccounts, preventing etcd rejections in high-churn namespaces (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/issues/1640[#1640]).

.Project cloning succeeds with nested clonePath values

Project cloning no longer fails when a nested `clonePath` is used and intermediate parent directories do not exist (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1652[#1652]).

.PVC cleanup Job pods inherit workspace podSecurityContext

PVC cleanup Job pods inherit the workspace `podSecurityContext` to match workspace deployment behavior (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1638[#1638]).

.Higher default memory limits for init-persistent-home container

The default `init-persistent-home` container memory limit is increased from 128Mi to 256Mi and the request from 64Mi to 128Mi to prevent OOM failures with large developer images (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1644[#1644]).

.Ephemeral workspaces mount emptyDir home volume with custom init-persistent-home

Ephemeral workspaces mount an `emptyDir` home volume when a custom `init-persistent-home` init container is configured and `persistUserHome` is enabled (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1649[#1649]).

DevWorkspace Operator 0.42.0 introduces configurable field-level restrictions for container and pod overrides, along with fixes for OpenShift registry RoleBinding accumulation, nested project cloning, PVC cleanup pod security context, init-persistent-home memory limits, and ephemeral workspace home volumes.

.Configurable field-level restrictions for container and pod overrides

Cluster administrators can now define deny rules in `DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig` to block specific fields or field values from being set via the `container-overrides` and `pod-overrides` DevWorkspace attributes. Restrictions are specified using the new `config.overrides.restrictedContainerOverrideFields` and `config.overrides.restrictedPodOverrideFields` fields.

On Kubernetes, a set of security-sensitive fields are denied out of the box including privileged containers, running as root, host networking, and `hostPath` volumes—matching the restrictions that OpenShift enforces natively via SCCs. These defaults can be adjusted from the global `DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig` object.

[source,yaml]
----
apiVersion: controller.devfile.io/v1alpha1
kind: DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig
metadata:
  name: devworkspace-operator-config
  namespace: $OPERATOR_INSTALL_NAMESPACE
config:
  overrides:
    restrictedContainerOverrideFields:
      - securityContext.privileged
      - securityContext.runAsUser
    restrictedPodOverrideFields:
      - hostNetwork
----

See link:https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/blob/main/docs/dwo-configuration.md#restricting-override-fields[restricting override fields] for configuration details.

.Fix OpenShift registry image-puller RoleBinding accumulating deleted workspace ServiceAccounts

OpenShift registry image-puller RoleBindings no longer accumulate deleted workspace ServiceAccounts, preventing etcd rejections in high-churn namespaces (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/issues/1640[#1640]).

.Fix project cloning failing when a nested clonePath is used

Project cloning no longer fails when a nested `clonePath` is used and intermediate parent directories do not exist (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1652[#1652]).

.Apply workspace podSecurityContext to PVC cleanup Job pods

PVC cleanup Job pods now inherit the workspace `podSecurityContext` to match workspace deployment behavior (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1638[#1638]).

.Increase default init-persistent-home container memory limits

The default `init-persistent-home` container memory limit is increased from 128Mi to 256Mi and the request from 64Mi to 128Mi to prevent OOM failures with large developer images (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1644[#1644]).

.Mount emptyDir home volume for ephemeral workspaces with custom init-persistent-home

Ephemeral workspaces now mount an `emptyDir` home volume when a custom `init-persistent-home` init container is configured and `persistUserHome` is enabled (https://github.com/devfile/devworkspace-operator/pull/1649[#1649]).

items.toString: devworkspace-webhook-server DWOC nodeSelector not applied via GitOps — oc rollout restart ineffective due to OLM, webhook management is startup-only

items.fromString:
h3. *Description of problem:*

 When DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig (DWOC) with {{config.webhook.nodeSelector}} is applied via GitOps (ArgoCD), the devworkspace-webhook-server deployment never receives the {{nodeSelector/tolerations}}, even after following the documented procedure ("restart the controller-manager").

 *Root cause (confirmed via investigation):*
  1. OLM installs the operator → creates webhook deployment at T=0 (no nodeSelector, before DWOC exists)
  2. ArgoCD applies DWOC at T+2m43s
  3. Controller-manager reads DWOC at startup and logs "Updated config" — but does NOT update the already-existing webhook deployment (webhook management is startup-only, no reconciliation loop)
  4. oc rollout restart is annulled by OLM — OLM reverts the new ReplicaSet to 0 replicas, keeping the original pod. The "restart" never actually happens.
  
  *What does NOT work:*

* oc rollout restart deployment/devworkspace-controller-manager → OLM reverts (ReplicaSet stays at 0 replicas)
* Deleting the webhook deployment alone → NOT recreated (no reconciliation loop watching it)


  *What works:*

* oc delete pod <controller-manager-pod> → OLM recreates pod via existing RS → new startup reads DWOC → recreates webhook deployment WITH nodeSelector ✅

*Documentation gap*: The official docs say "terminate the controller-manager pod and restart it" which is correct, but using oc rollout restart (the standard OCP command) does NOT work because OLM intercepts and reverts it. The correct method is oc delete pod, which is not explicitly documented.

h3. Description of problem:

When DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig (DWOC) with config.webhook.nodeSelector is deployed via GitOps (ArgoCD/OpenShift GitOps), the devworkspace-webhook-server deployment never receives the nodeSelector/tolerations. Following the documented procedure ("terminate the controller-manager pod and restart it") using oc rollout restart does NOT work because OLM intercepts and reverts the rolling update.

h3. Workaround

Delete the controller-manager pod directly (NOT oc rollout restart). OLM recreates it using the existing ReplicaSet. The new pod reads the DWOC at startup and recreates the webhook deployment with the correct nodeSelector/tolerations:

{code:bash}oc delete pod -n openshift-dev-terminal \
  $(oc get pods -n openshift-dev-terminal --no-headers | grep devworkspace-controller-manager | awk '{print $1}')
# Result: webhook pods rescheduled to infra nodes within ~30 seconds{code}

For GitOps automation: a Job that deletes the controller-manager pod after the DWOC is applied ensures correct placement on every fresh cluster install.

h3. Prerequisites (if any, like setup, operators/versions):

* OCP: 4.20.23 (IPI, AWS eu-central-1)
* DevWorkspace Operator: v0.41.0 (openshift-dev-terminal namespace)
* OpenShift GitOps: 1.20.4 (ArgoCD managing DWOC + operator Subscription in same Application)
* DWOC: config.webhook.nodeSelector: {node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: ""} + tolerations: [{key: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra, operator: Exists}]
* Infra nodes tainted with: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=:NoSchedule

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Deploy DWO via GitOps: OLM Subscription + DevWorkspaceOperatorConfig in the same ArgoCD Application
# Set DWOC config.webhook.nodeSelector to target infra nodes (e.g. node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: "")
# Observe that devworkspace-webhook-server deployment has no nodeSelector/tolerations
# Try the documented fix: oc rollout restart deployment/devworkspace-controller-manager
# Observe webhook deployment still has no nodeSelector after rollout restart

h3. Actual results:

* devworkspace-webhook-server deployment has no nodeSelector/tolerations after DWOC creation
* oc rollout restart is silently reverted by OLM: a new ReplicaSet is created but stays at 0 replicas; the original pod continues running
* Deleting the webhook deployment alone does NOT trigger recreation (no continuous reconciliation loop in controller-manager)
* Root cause: OLM installs operator at T=0 (no nodeSelector), ArgoCD applies DWOC at T+2m43s; webhook management runs ONLY at startup, not via reconciliation loop

h3. Expected results:

* The controller-manager should reconcile the webhook deployment continuously when DWOC changes (not only at startup), OR
* The documentation should explicitly state that oc rollout restart does NOT work when OLM manages the operator, and that oc delete pod must be used instead

h3. Reproducibility (Always/Intermittent/Only Once):

Always — 100% reproducible on any OCP cluster with infra nodes where DWO is deployed via GitOps and DWOC is applied after operator installation.

h3. Acceptance criteria:

* devworkspace-webhook-server deployment receives nodeSelector/tolerations from DWOC without requiring manual pod deletion
* OR: documentation updated to clarify oc rollout restart is ineffective under OLM and oc delete pod is the correct procedure

h3. Definition of Done:

* Fix verified on OCP 4.20+ with infra nodes and GitOps deployment
* No manual intervention required after fresh cluster install via GitOps

h3. Build Details:

* OCP version: 4.20.23
* DevWorkspace Operator: v0.41.0 (devworkspace-operator.v0.41.0)
* OpenShift GitOps: 1.20.4 (openshift-gitops-operator.v1.20.4)

h3. Additional info (Such as Logs, Screenshots, etc):

Timing race confirmed via timestamps:

{noformat}T=09:55:43  OLM installs operator, controller-manager starts
T=09:55:50  Webhook deployment created (no nodeSelector — DWOC does not exist yet)
T=09:58:33  ArgoCD applies DWOC (2m43s later)
T=09:58:33  Controller-manager logs: "Updated config to [webhook.nodeSelectors=[node-role.kubernetes.io/infra=]...]"
            → config updated IN MEMORY only, webhook deployment NOT updated

oc rollout restart behavior:
  → New ReplicaSet created (7f59d69fdb, 4m39s age)
  → OLM immediately scales new RS to 0, keeps original pod running
  → oc rollout status incorrectly reports "successfully rolled out"{noformat}

Related tickets: CRW-6232 (webhook placement feature), CRW-9297 (infra node placement, closed)

= Integrate AI coding assistants into the development workflow

To enable AI-assisted development in cloud workspaces, administrators can configure AI coding tool providers in a labeled ConfigMap and make them available to developers through the {prod-short} Dashboard. Developers can select an AI provider when creating a workspace, manage API keys in User Preferences, and view or change the active AI tool on existing workspaces.

.AI provider and tool configuration

Administrators define AI providers and tools in a ConfigMap with the labels `app.kubernetes.io/component: ai-tool-registry` and `app.kubernetes.io/part-of: che.eclipse.org`. The Dashboard discovers the ConfigMap by these labels, so the ConfigMap name can be any valid value. Multiple tools can share one provider. Tool definitions, including provider configurations and injector image references, are maintained in the link:https://github.com/che-incubator/che-ai-tool-images[che-ai-tool-images] repository.

.AI provider selector on workspace creation

The Get Started page includes a selector for AI providers. The selected provider ID is passed as a factory URL parameter (`ai-provider=`) and the tool is injected into the DevWorkspace at creation time.

.API key management in User Preferences

An *AI Providers Keys* tab in User Preferences allows developers to list, add, update, and delete API keys. Keys are stored as Kubernetes Secrets with auto-mount labels so the DevWorkspace Controller injects them as environment variables.

.AI tool info on Workspace Details

The Workspace Details Overview tab shows the currently injected AI tool. Developers can view available tools and switch to a different one when the workspace is stopped.

[IMPORTANT]
====
Integrating AI coding assistants into the development workflow is a Technology Preview feature only. Technology Preview features are not supported with Red Hat production service level agreements (SLAs) and might not be functionally complete. Red Hat does not recommend using them in production. These features provide early access to upcoming product features, enabling customers to test functionality and provide feedback during the development process.

There is a known issue where connecting to Dev Spaces workspaces from local IDEs using SSH fails when the workspace is based on UBI 9 images. 1. Update your devfile to reference the latest UBI 9 base image
2. Restart your workspace to apply the updated base image
3. Reconnect from your local IDE using SSH
